findings.disposition: The correction remains visually effective on the exact integrated source. Wrapped SVG and emoji cues align with the first line and native desktop/compact title owners show no renewed vertical offset. The current unchanged Storybook plays passed their geometry and bounds assertions; visual inspection does not substitute unrecorded numerical pixel measurements.

The native fixture Name field remains square/default-styled compared with the rounded production form. This pre-existing fixture styling difference is outside the title alignment repair. Do not describe these compact previews as pixel-identical production forms or as evidence that this difference was fixed.

observations.wrapping: Real multiline titles remain legible and contained, including five-line destructive text on phone. Cues follow the first line rather than the whole text block.
observations.controls: Close controls on shared modals, and native Cancel/Make a copy controls and form fields, remain visible and contained. Visible focus rings or selected text are preserved.
observations.contrast: No new visual contrast or glyph-legibility issue observed in the light and dark captures. This statement is visual review, not a newly performed WCAG contrast measurement.
observations.nativeOwnership: Desktop and compact SDK layouts are actual opened owners from the unmodified hosted build, not duplicate mocked dialogs.

personas.Owner: Long destructive questions, copy title and selected form values remain readable without hiding actions on phone.
personas.Collaborator: Cue and title remain distinct while explanatory copy and form controls stay readable; this review claims no change to access authority.
personas.Operator: Shared title behavior remains consistent with the previously inspected unchanged administration owners, and the capture completed below the existing 2 GiB limit without introducing product complexity.
personas.Link guest: Phone wrapping and readable text remain usable without relying on the decorative cue as the accessible name; no guest access expansion is claimed.
